title: Choice-family identity for Gowers norms
statement: Let $n,k$ be natural numbers and let $f,g:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb R$, where $\mathbb F_2$ is the two-element field. For each subset $A$ of $\mathbb F_2^k$, choose the function equal to $f$ on indices in $A$ and to $g$ on the other indices; the sum over all such $A$ of the product, over $s\in\mathbb F_2^k$, of the Gowers $k$-norm of the chosen function at index $s$ equals $(\|f\|_{U^k}+\|g\|_{U^k})^{2^k}$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ and $g$ are real-valued functions on $\mathbb F_2^n$
caveat: The defined Gowers norm is the diagonal inner average raised to the power $1/2^k$; for some inputs its value need not be nonnegative, so interpreting it as the conventional nonnegative Gowers norm could misstate the formal definition.
